text:
alex: heads up — found a correctness window with prefix + tombstone interplay during eviction. quick description: client writes key K under prefix P, we ack write, then eviction kicks and drops P entries, background compaction later applies a tombstone for K (from GC path) and then a read comes back and gets a stale miss. curious about short-term mitigations before we do a larger refactor.

maria: ouch. can you repro reliably in a stress test? is it specific to our lazy tombstone apply path? :thinking:

alex: repro is intermittent but deterministic if you force eviction between write ack and compaction. sequence: write -> ack -> eviction evicts prefix (no pin) -> compaction task runs on node B and writes tombstone to backing store -> read routed to node A which doesn't have prefix and returns miss. we rely on sequencer to order writes but eviction+compaction break the in-memory invariant.

devon: so the core is a visibility gap caused by eviction removing in-memory committed state before tombstone propagation is globally visible. options: 1) pin-on-write short lease; 2) write-through to backing store and treat in-memory eviction as a cache only; 3) attach version vectors to prefixes and require read to check backing store if version mismatch; 4) eagerly replicate tombstone application via sequencer before ack. tradeoffs: latency vs complexity.

sam: +1 for pin-on-write as low-risk patch. pin duration can be tiny (e.g., 500ms) and configurable per tenant. cheap and fixes most interleavings. downside: lots of short pins could blow memory under high write QPS.

maria: pin-on-write still relies on routing correctness. if read gets sent to another shard that never had prefix, pin won't help. we'd need a global lease or sequencer-mediated pin.

alex: right — our current lease is local to shard. we could do a short global write-lease via sequencer: require sequencer to emit a side-channel "recent-write" marker for prefix for X ms; reads that miss in-memory consult sequencer for recent-write bit before returning miss. cheap to implement since sequencer already orders writes.

devon: sequencer consult adds one RPC on misses. doesn't impact steady-state read hits. seems reasonable.

sam: other risk — tombstone creation path: compaction writes tombstones as metadata later. Could we make compaction tombstones use a tombstone-epoch > last-write-epoch so reads can detect staleness? e.g., attach epoch to tombstone and have read path compare against prefix version vector.

alex: that would require versioning everywhere, big refactor. prefer incremental: (A) sequencer recent-write marker + (B) small pin-on-write if sequencer is slow. fallback: read-miss triggers a quick backing-store check if recent-write marker set.

maria: sounds pragmatic. need an experiment/bench: measure additional P99 latency for read-miss that checks sequencer or backing store. also simulate high write QPS to see pin overhead.

devon: I'll prototype sequencer marker at the sequencer-client level: when we commit a write for prefix P, emit an ephemeral map entry (prefix->ts) stored in sequencer memcache; reads can query sequencer for marker presence. TTL tuned by metrics.

sam: FYI ops-bot: create ticket for proto + bench + rollout plan? @ops-bot any suggestions for rollout gates?

ops-bot: ticket created INC-4521: "prefix shadow/tombstone visibility fix - sequencer marker prototype". assign: devon. rollouts: start in canary region, track read-miss latencies, read consistency regressions, pin memory usage. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks. follow-ups: add a unit test forcing eviction+compaction interleaving, add chaos test for routing to different nodes, and table of expected SLO impacts for different TTL choices. I'll draft the doc RFE tonight and tag you all.
